title: Retain Font Attribute for Preposition

illustrates.quote: Follow print when a title is printed in italics or other emphasizing typeface and follows a preposition that is in a different typeface, or when the preposition is in a typeface different from the title.

blocks.features: Centered, plain roman title, not italicized (the reverse pairing from Example 5-11).
Centered subtitle: 'from' italic, book title 'Seabiscuit: An American Legend' plain roman — the preposition, not the title, carries the differing typeface, per 5.4.2's second clause.
Plain roman opening line; the braille excerpt truncates after 'settled over', short of the print's fuller sentence.

print.notes: Companion example to 5-11: here the preposition ('from'), not the title, carries the differing typeface.
print.surroundingText: Follows rule 5.4.2's example pair, immediately after Example 5-11, on the same printed page (5-8).
print.printFeatures: Plain (unboxed) centered title block, matching Example 5-11's layout; mixed-typeface subtitle (italic preposition + plain title).

braille.notes: Eight lines, margin 8 stripped. Line 1 blank filler; line 2 centered title (indent 10), no typeform indicator — heading font attributes ignored, per 5.3.1; line 3 centered subtitle (indent 12) with a single-word italic indicator ('.1') directly before 'f' (from) only, confirming only the single word 'from' is italicized; line 4, 'An American Legend' (indent 10), continues unmarked; line 5 blank (interior); line 6 centered byline (indent 5); line 7 blank (interior); line 8 paragraph opening, ending '444' (an ellipsis/continuation marker) — the print's fuller sentence ('... the Howard barn in the week before the Santa Anita Handicap.') is not transcribed in this worked excerpt, a deliberate excerpt truncation in the source, not an omission introduced here.

uncertain: The print sentence continues well past what the braille excerpt transcribes (it stops at 'settled over' plus an ellipsis marker); the remainder has no braille counterpart in the source to check against.
resolution: Both runs agree on braille byte-for-byte and on the substantive print facts. Heading level (1, centered) verified directly against the (40−len)//2 formula for all three centered lines (title indent 10/len 20; subtitle line1 indent 12/len 15; subtitle line2 indent 10/len 19; byline indent 5/len 30 — all match exactly).
